digest.overview:
The Supreme Court ruled that the Trump administration must keep providing gender-affirming care to federal inmates while a legal challenge proceeds. The Justice Department began notifying counties where it wants to monitor next month's elections, and the top Democrats on the House and Senate intelligence committees said they are preparing for President Trump to claim foreign meddling. AIPAC said it will stop endorsing candidates and giving directly to campaigns, though its super PAC will keep operating. A new poll found record support for Democratic congressional candidates. Justice Elena Kagan said the Supreme Court is undermining voting rights. Israeli forces detained and then released dozens of Americans, including New York congressional nominee Brad Lander, who were helping Palestinian olive harvesters in the West Bank. A strengthening nor'easter lashed the Mid-Atlantic coast with violent surf and coastal flooding.

Abroad, Vladimir Putin told U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff he agrees in principle to resume three-way peace talks with Ukraine and the U.S., and a Kremlin aide said they could restart around Nov. 10, possibly in Abu Dhabi. North Korea said it will resume propaganda broadcasts across the border, and Kim Yo Jong said its loudspeakers will be ready to operate within days. Saudi Arabia canceled its "Davos in the Desert" investor conference because of Houthi strikes from Yemen, as Britain offered military support. A severe security flaw in the widely used PHP software prompted South Korea to launch an emergency response. A new U.N. report found that current policies put the world on track for 2.8 degrees Celsius of warming this century.

Anthony Edwards poured in 45 points as Minnesota won 131–106 in Miami, spoiling Giannis Antetokounmpo's 35-point Heat debut, and the Lakers routed the Warriors 127–105 on a packed opening Wednesday. Golden State is reportedly exploring trades for Kristaps Porziņģis, and the 76ers host the Cavaliers tonight. In the NFL, Week 7 opens tonight with the Patriots at the Bears, the league said it will not punish the Eagles over Jalen Hurts' blood clots, and Washington lost Terry McLaurin for the season. Patrick Mahomes practiced fully on Wednesday. Baseball is in its final pause before the World Series starts Friday, with the Rays at the Brewers.

Bayern and Arsenal drew 2–2 in Munich behind a Harry Kane penalty, while Real Madrid beat RB Leipzig 4–1 and Aston Villa beat Viking 3–1, leaving five clubs perfect after three Champions League games. Como stunned Manchester United 4–1 and Galatasaray won 4–2 at Lille. The Europa and Conference leagues play tonight, with Milan at Bournemouth and Brighton at Jablonec, before Sunday's El Clásico at Barcelona. St. Louis City won the U.S. Open Cup on penalties against Columbus, and FC Seoul can clinch the K League 1 title against Gangwon on Saturday. In the KBO, Kia opens the second round at Samsung on Sunday.

articles.title: France Imposes Partial Curfews After Police 'Lost Control' of Protests

articles.summary: A car struck an Australian independent federal lawmaker, critically injuring her in what the prime minister called a deliberate attack; the driver was arrested.
articles.title: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
